title: dev.qory.session.exited
description: A session of the run ended: its runtime exited, the session stopped it, or the join was refused. One per join, the last event of the session's, after its dev.qory.session.started; a refused join has no dev.qory.session.started, and its dev.qory.session.exited is failed with exit_code -1 and the refusal's code as reason. The run stays open after it: only dev.qory.run.exited ends the run. The runtime's exit decides the state: succeeded on exit status 0, with no reason and no signal; failed on any other exit status or a signal, with no reason; cancelled with timeout, the run's time limit, or interrupted, a stop from where the run was started, whatever the exit status or signal. When the gateway ends the run while a session runs, the gateway's dev.qory.run.exited is the run's last event, and that session has no dev.qory.session.exited in the run's stream.

session.description: The session's number in the run, from 1: the one of its dev.qory.session.started, or for a join the gateway refused, the number the gateway gave the join request.

state.description: How the session ended: succeeded, failed or cancelled, as the runtime's exit and the reason decide it.

exit_code.description: The runtime's exit status, or -1 when a signal killed it, and -1 for a refused join, whose runtime never started.

signal.description: The signal that killed the runtime, when one did: SIGKILL, SIGTERM.

reason.description: Why the session ended, when it ended other than by the runtime exiting by itself: timeout, the run's time limit was reached and the session stopped the runtime; interrupted, the run was stopped from where it was started, a Ctrl-C or a signal to the program that runs the session, before the session observed the runtime's exit; or, for a refused join, the refusal's code, one the session decides itself, those of refusal.Decides. Absent when the runtime exited by itself.

duration_ms.description: Milliseconds from the session's dev.qory.session.started to its end; 0 for a refused join, which has none.
